meta.joinKey: worldAnchors joins to the zones field in proposals.json. Every tree is acquired through a quest chain that runs through named vanilla locations, which is the seam between the two documents: one describes the world, the other describes something you go into that world to get.

structure.rows: Seven. Row one is free, each subsequent row needs five more points spent in the tree. Row seven unlocks at thirty.
structure.mark: The twenty-point talent. The hybrid's prize, usable without deep investment. A splash is a character, not a broken build.
structure.capstone: The thirty-one point talent. Transformative, something a character either has or does not.
structure.localMechanic: No absorbed tree imports a new resource bar. Each layers a tree-local mechanic on the host's existing resource, the way combo points and soul shards already do.
structure.verbs: Acquisition differs per tree so seven chains do not feel like seven copies of one quest: forged, taught, taken, fallen, earned, granted, copied.

statusKey.committed: argued and integrated into the class document
statusKey.candidate: proposed, not yet decided; see two-trees.md

sourceKey.absorbed: a post-vanilla class or spec brought in as a tree
sourceKey.original: no retail source; built from vanilla lore the game asserts and never shows

trees.name: Blackguard
trees.concept: The Light turned inward. Self-sustain becomes leeching, blessings become presences that cannot be shared, and the aura harms instead of helps.
trees.retailSource: Death Knight, Blood plus the core fallen-knight identity
trees.localMechanic: Blight, a disease applied by Blackguard strikes that roughly a third of the tree pays out against
trees.verbNote: The only tree that should be done to the character rather than by them. A paladin does not apply to become a death knight.
trees.professionNote: Deliberately none. The whole point of the fallen verb is that nothing is prepared and nothing is chosen.
trees.permanentCost: Loses the ability to cast Blessings or direct heals on other players.
trees.loreAnchor: Arthas was a paladin. The Death Knight fantasy is the paladin fantasy corrupted, and Warcraft III spends an entire campaign on the transition.

talents.name: Unholy Vigor
talents.text: Increases melee damage by 1/2/3/4/5%.

talents.name: Grave Cold
talents.text: Reduces the mana cost of Blackguard abilities by 5/10/15%.

talents.name: Deathward
talents.text: Reduces Shadow and Frost damage taken by 2/4/6/8/10%.

talents.name: Plague Strike
talents.text: Instant melee strike dealing weapon damage and applying Blight for 15 sec. The tree's enabler.

talents.name: Deathchill
talents.text: Blight also slows movement by 15/30%.

talents.name: Rotting Flesh
talents.text: Blighted targets have their armor reduced by 2/4/6%.

talents.name: Morbid Strength
talents.text: Increases attack power by 8/16/24/32/40.

talents.name: Leeching Blade
talents.text: Melee attacks against Blighted targets heal you for 1/2/3/4/5% of damage dealt.

talents.name: Spreading Corruption
talents.text: Blight has a 50/100% chance to spread to a nearby enemy every 5 sec.

talents.name: Chilblain
talents.text: Plague Strike has a 10/20/30% chance to refund its mana cost.

talents.name: Presence of the Grave
talents.text: Replaces your active Blessing with a self-only presence granting armor and health regeneration. While active you cannot cast Blessings on others.

talents.name: Chill of the Grave
talents.text: Blight reduces healing received by 10/20/30%.

talents.name: Necrotic Aura
talents.text: Enemies within 8 yards take 2/4/6 Shadow damage every 3 sec.

talents.name: Vile Contagion
talents.text: Increases Blight duration by 3/6 sec.

talents.name: Blood Rite
talents.text: Consumes all Blight on a target to instantly heal you for a large amount. Off the global cooldown.
talents.note: Lay on Hands inverted. An emergency heal that requires you to have poisoned somebody first, which is a complete character in one talent.

talents.name: Unyielding Dead
talents.text: Reduces the chance to be critically hit by 1/2/3%.

talents.name: Corpsefeeder
talents.text: Blood Rite also removes one poison or disease from you, 50/100% chance.

talents.name: Frozen Heart
talents.text: Reduces damage taken by 2/4/6% while Presence of the Grave is active.

talents.name: Reaping
talents.text: Killing a Blighted enemy grants 10/20% attack speed for 10 sec.

talents.name: Death's Advance
talents.text: Increases movement speed by 5/10/15% and reduces snare duration by 15/30/45%.

talents.name: Damnation
talents.text: Permanent. Your Seals become Plagues, melee attacks apply Blight automatically, and Leeching Blade's healing is doubled. Your appearance changes and does not change back. You can no longer cast Blessings or direct heals on other players.

trees.name: Necromancy
trees.concept: The fourth school. A caster who raises the disposable dead, spreads plague, and drains.
trees.retailSource: Necromancer as a Warcraft III unit, plus Unholy Death Knight's caster half
trees.localMechanic: The Risen, skeletal minions raised from corpses, plural and expiring
trees.verbNote: Necromancy in Warcraft is explicitly curriculum. Somebody teaches it, in a building, to students.
trees.professionNote: For the plague components. Scholomance is as much a laboratory as a school. Satisfiable by another player, never required personally.
trees.loreAnchor: Kel'Thuzad was a Dalaran mage and a member of the Kirin Tor before founding the Cult of the Damned. Both endpoints of that career change are already in the game.

talents.name: Shadow Focus
talents.text: Increases shadow damage by 2/4/6/8/10%.

talents.name: Grave Robbing
talents.text: Reduces the mana cost of Necromancy spells by 5/10/15%.

talents.name: Deathchill Focus
talents.text: Reduces the chance your Necromancy spells are resisted by 2/4/6/8/10%.

talents.name: Wither
talents.text: A shadow damage over time effect. Mage's first real DoT and the tree's rhythm-setter.

talents.name: Bone Chill
talents.text: Wither reduces the target's attack speed by 10/20%.

talents.name: Rotting Touch
talents.text: Wither deals 4/8/12% additional damage to targets below 35% health.

talents.name: Dark Intellect
talents.text: Increases Intellect by 1/2/3/4/5%.

talents.name: Siphon Life
talents.text: Wither heals you for 5/10/15/20/25% of the damage it deals.

talents.name: Corpse Harvest
talents.text: Enemies you kill leave a corpse for 30/60 sec.

talents.name: Sepulchral Study
talents.text: Reduces the cast time of Necromancy spells by 0.1/0.2/0.3 sec.

talents.name: Bone Armor
talents.text: Surrounds you with bone fragments absorbing damage. Each absorb consumes a fragment, so the shield visibly depletes.

talents.name: Contagion
talents.text: Wither spreads to a nearby enemy on the target's death, 33/66/100% chance.

talents.name: Boneyard
talents.text: Corpse Harvest also has a 15/30/45% chance to leave a corpse when a party member scores a killing blow.

talents.name: Withering Cold
talents.text: Wither slows casting speed by 10/20%.

talents.name: Raise Skeleton
talents.text: Consumes a corpse to raise a skeletal minion for 60 sec. One at a time.
talents.note: The largest mark in the document, because vanilla mage has no pet at all. The corpse requirement keeps it tied to combat that already happened.

talents.name: Grave Chill
talents.text: Bone Armor also reduces the attack speed of melee attackers by 5/10/15%.

talents.name: Necrotic Aptitude
talents.text: Increases Risen duration by 15/30 sec.

talents.name: Unstable Dead
talents.text: Your Risen explode on expiry for 33/66/100% of a Wither tick to all nearby enemies.

talents.name: Dark Command
talents.text: Increases Risen damage by 15/30%.

talents.name: Death Pact
talents.text: Consuming a Risen heals you for 10/20/30% of your health.

talents.name: Command the Damned
talents.text: Raise Skeleton no longer requires a corpse and you may sustain three Risen at once. They still expire, and they always will.
talents.note: The expiry is the identity, not a balance lever. Warlocks have a companion. Necromancers have ammunition.

trees.name: Metamorphosis
trees.concept: The caster who becomes the thing they summon.
trees.retailSource: Demon Hunter, Vengeance. Previously a Demonology warlock talent from Wrath through Warlords.
trees.localMechanic: Fel corruption, a self-applied stacking state, plus the form itself at the bottom
trees.verbNote: Nobody grants this and nobody teaches it. The warlock performs a ritual on themselves and it works or it does not.
trees.professionNote: Tailoring fits the Season of Discovery precedent of cloth built for tanking. Enchanting for the ritual components.
trees.permanentCost: Marked by the fel in a visible, permanent, mechanically minor way.
trees.loreAnchor: Metamorphosis is adapted from the Warcraft III Demon Hunter ability, visually based on Illidan, and was removed from warlocks in patch 7.0.3 specifically to make room for the Demon Hunter class.

talents.name: Fel Vigor
talents.text: Increases Fire and Shadow damage by 1/2/3/4/5%.

talents.name: Demonic Hide
talents.text: Increases armor from items by 3/6/9%.

talents.name: Fel Concentration
talents.text: Reduces spell pushback by 14/28/42/56/70%.

talents.name: Shadow Cleave
talents.text: A short-range shadow attack striking up to three enemies in front of you. Works out of form, better in it.

talents.name: Fel Stamina
talents.text: Increases total health by 3/6%.

talents.name: Cruel Intent
talents.text: Increases Shadow Cleave damage by 4/8/12%.

talents.name: Demonic Bulwark
talents.text: Increases block value by 4/8/12/16/20%.

talents.name: Demonic Aegis
talents.text: Reduces physical damage taken by 1/2/3/4/5%.

talents.name: Soul Link
talents.text: A portion of damage taken is redirected to your demon.

talents.name: Master Summoner
talents.text: Reduces the cast time of summoning spells by 2/4/6 sec.

talents.name: Immolation Aura
talents.text: Deals periodic fire damage to nearby enemies and generates threat.

talents.name: Fel Resilience
talents.text: Reduces the duration of stun and snare effects by 10/20/30%.

talents.name: Unholy Sacrifice
talents.text: Sacrificing your demon grants a shield absorbing 10/20/30% more.

talents.name: Fel Ferocity
talents.text: Increases the critical strike chance of Shadow Cleave by 3/6%.

talents.name: Fel Aegis
talents.text: Partial transformation for 20 sec on a 3 minute cooldown. Large armor bonus, increased threat, cheaper Shadow Cleave.
talents.note: This is Wrath's Metamorphosis, which was a three minute cooldown. The capstone is Season of Discovery's, which is permanent. Splitting them across the two slots is not a compromise between the versions, it is both of them in the order they were built.

talents.name: Demonic Knowledge
talents.text: Increases spell damage by 3/6/9% of your demon's Stamina.

talents.name: Warding Fel
talents.text: Reduces magic damage taken by 3/6%.

talents.name: Unending Fel
talents.text: Reduces Fel Aegis cooldown by 20/40/60 sec.

talents.name: Demonic Fury
talents.text: Shadow Cleave generates 50/100% additional threat.

talents.name: Fel Domination
talents.text: Immolation Aura generates 20/40/60% more threat.

talents.name: Metamorphosis
talents.text: Permanent demon form. Armor multiplied substantially, Shadow Bolt replaced by Shadow Cleave, all threat multiplied. You look like this now.

trees.name: Bladedancer
trees.concept: Mobile melee flow. Glaives, fists, and open hands, spread across several targets rather than concentrated on one.
trees.retailSource: Demon Hunter Havoc merged with Windwalker Monk
trees.localMechanic: Momentum, a stacking state gained by moving and by striking new targets, lost by standing still. Combo points remain the spend.
trees.verbNote: The rogue watches someone fight and learns it by imitation. The least mystical acquisition on the list and the most in character.
trees.professionNote: For the glaives and the harness.
trees.worldAnchorGap: Unspecified. Section 8.6 names chains for Blackguard, Necromancy, Metamorphosis, and Runeblade only. This is an open item.
trees.loreAnchor: The Blademaster and the Aldrachi glaive tradition are both available as naming material without importing the Illidari. The Pandaren Brewmaster was a hireable Warcraft III neutral hero, not a race requirement.

weaponFork.note: The tree does not ask which fantasy you are. Your main hand answers. Vanilla already gates Backstab and Ambush on daggers and carries per-weapon specialization talents in Combat, so this is the existing rule rather than a new one.
weaponFork.bladed: One-handed swords, axes, daggers. Forward, thrown, burst. Reads as the duelist.
weaponFork.fist: Fist weapons or unarmed. Around you, sustained, continuous. Reads as the martial artist.

forks.bladed: A 15 yard forward leap on a 20 sec cooldown. A gap closer.
forks.fist: An 8 yard roll in any direction on an 8 sec cooldown. Repositioning.

forks.bladed: An arc striking enemies in a cone in front of you at up to 8 yards.
forks.fist: A spin striking every enemy within melee range around you.

forks.bladed: Momentum is consumed by your next finisher for a large burst, then resets.
forks.fist: Momentum has no cap and does not decay while you keep moving.

weaponFork.consequence: Swapping weapons swaps the style in the field, so a player carrying both is carrying two builds at the cost of a weapon swap rather than a respec. It also gives fist weapons a reason to exist, which vanilla's thin fist itemization currently does not provide.

talents.name: Flowing Form
talents.text: Increases damage with fist weapons and unarmed attacks by 2/4/6/8/10%.

talents.name: Fleet Footed
talents.text: Increases movement speed by 3/6/9%.

talents.name: Deft Hands
talents.text: Increases attack speed with fist weapons and one-handed blades by 2/4/6/8/10%.

talents.name: Tumble
talents.text: A short directional roll. Not a sprint. The thing that makes the fantasy read as flow rather than speed.

talents.name: Open Hand
talents.text: Your unarmed attacks use your Fist Weapon skill and scale as a weapon.
talents.note: Vanilla ships an Unarmed weapon skill that exists, can be levelled, and is pointless. One talent makes it real in exactly one tree.

talents.name: Lithe
talents.text: Reduces the cooldown of Tumble by 1/2/3 sec.

talents.name: Sinew
talents.text: Increases Agility by 1/2/3/4/5%.

talents.name: Momentum
talents.text: Moving in combat grants a stack every 2 sec, up to five, each increasing damage by 1/2/3/4/5%. Standing still for 3 sec clears them.

talents.name: No Opening Needed
talents.text: Your opener abilities no longer require stealth, at 50/100% effectiveness.

talents.name: Redirection
talents.text: Changing targets no longer clears combo points, 33/66/100% of the time.

talents.name: Sweeping Kick
talents.text: A combo point spender that briefly stuns all enemies within melee range. Rogue's first multi-target control.

talents.name: Blade Harmony
talents.text: Attacking a target you have not hit in the last 6 sec grants a combo point, 33/66/100% chance.

talents.name: Precision Footwork
talents.text: Increases chance to hit by 1/2/3%.

talents.name: Second Wind
talents.text: Tumble restores 10/20 energy.

talents.name: Whirling Blades
talents.text: A finisher dealing damage to multiple enemies, scaling with combo points.
talents.note: Rogue's entire vanilla identity is single-target burst from stealth. A multi-target finisher is the largest thing twenty points could buy.

talents.name: Unbroken Rhythm
talents.text: Reduces the energy cost of Whirling Blades by 5/10/15.

talents.name: Evasive
talents.text: Increases dodge chance by 1/2% per Momentum stack, up to 5/10%.

talents.name: Edged Discipline
talents.text: Bladed only. Whirling Blades may be used at range, striking a cone from where it lands.

talents.name: Flowing Palm
talents.text: Fist or unarmed only. Whirling Blades refunds a combo point for every two targets struck.

talents.name: Relentless
talents.text: Whirling Blades refunds one combo point per 2/3/4 targets struck.

talents.name: Uninterrupted
talents.text: Momentum stacks decay one at a time rather than clearing.

talents.name: Killing Flow
talents.text: Killing an enemy grants two Momentum stacks, 33/66/100% chance.

talents.name: Unending Dance
talents.text: Momentum behaves differently by weapon. Whirling Blades no longer costs a full finisher below three targets.
talents.note: The duelist builds and spends. The martial artist accumulates and never stops. That is the difference between the two fantasies stated mechanically; everything else is presentation.

trees.name: Conduit
trees.concept: Elemental power held rather than thrown, and given to a person rather than to the ground.
trees.retailSource: Evoker, all three specs, with Augmentation as the load-bearing one
trees.localMechanic: Empowerment, where certain spells may be held while casting to advance through charge stages
trees.verbNote: The elements agree or they do not, so the chain is a petition rather than a conquest. It should be possible to be refused and have to return.
trees.professionNote: None. Nothing is crafted and nothing is bought.
trees.worldAnchorGap: Unspecified. Elemental sites would be the obvious home but Section 8.6 does not name them. Open item.
trees.loreAnchor: Dragonflight-era Evoker lore does not exist in a Classic timeframe and should not be imported. The shaman's existing relationship with the elements carries the whole tree.

talents.name: Elemental Focus
talents.text: Increases Nature and Frost damage by 1/2/3/4/5%.

talents.name: Steady Channel
talents.text: Reduces pushback while empowering by 33/66/100%.

talents.name: Elemental Warding
talents.text: Reduces Fire, Frost, and Nature damage taken by 2/4/6/8/10%.

talents.name: Empowered Lightning
talents.text: Lightning Bolt may be held to charge through three stages.

talents.name: Grounding
talents.text: Reduces the mana cost of empowered spells by 10/20%.

talents.name: Tidal Focus
talents.text: Reduces the mana cost of healing spells by 1/2/3%.

talents.name: Ancestral Insight
talents.text: Increases Intellect by 1/2/3/4/5%.

talents.name: Living Current
talents.text: Empowered spells at full charge restore 1/2/3/4/5% of base mana.

talents.name: Empowered Healing
talents.text: Healing Wave may be held to charge.

talents.name: Storm Reach
talents.text: Increases the range of empowered spells by 3/6/9 yards.

talents.name: Totemic Reach
talents.text: Your totems affect allies at twice the radius.

talents.name: Elemental Grace
talents.text: Empowerment charges 10/20/30% faster.

talents.name: Restorative Current
talents.text: Empowered Healing at full charge also heals a second nearby ally for 15/30/45%.

talents.name: Earthen Footing
talents.text: Reduces the chance to be interrupted while empowering by 35/70%.

talents.name: Elemental Bond
talents.text: Places one active totem's effect on a single ally instead of on the ground. The effect follows them and persists while they remain in your party.
talents.note: Augmentation translated into vanilla's vocabulary with no invention required. Shaman's defining contribution is already a buff placed on the ground; placing it on a person is one talent.

talents.name: Elemental Devotion
talents.text: Increases the duration of Elemental Bond by 5/10/15 sec.

talents.name: Surge
talents.text: Empowered spells at full charge have a 10/20% chance not to consume mana.

talents.name: Conductive
talents.text: Empowered spells at full charge also strike a second target for 20/40/60%.

talents.name: Deep Bond
talents.text: Elemental Bond effects are 15/30% stronger.

talents.name: Wellspring
talents.text: Living Current also restores mana to bonded allies at 25/50/75% of the amount.

talents.name: Confluence
talents.text: Elemental Bond may be active on up to three allies at once, and fully empowered spells grant a brief share of their effect to everyone you are bonded to.

trees.name: Runeblade
trees.concept: A warrior whose weapon is enchanted with cold. Not a caster, and deliberately smaller in ambition than the other six.
trees.localMechanic: Rune charges accumulated on the weapon and spent on effects. The magic belongs to the object throughout.
trees.verbNote: An object, not a power, which is the whole reason warrior can have it without becoming a spellcaster. The chain produces a weapon and requires someone who can make one.
trees.professionNote: The model for the rest. Not that the warrior must be a smith, but that they need access to one. Same as Thunderfury and the Sulfuron Hammer.
trees.loreAnchor: Runeblades are forged objects in Warcraft lore, so a warrior who carries one has acquired an item rather than a power. Warrior's identity in vanilla is defined negatively, as the class with no magic, and this respects that.

talents.name: Cold Iron
talents.text: Increases weapon damage by 1/2/3/4/5%.

talents.name: Frostbitten
talents.text: Increases Frost resistance by 5/10/15.

talents.name: Iron Discipline
talents.text: Increases the chance to hit with melee weapons by 1/2/3/4/5%.

talents.name: Rime
talents.text: Melee attacks have a 5/10% chance to slow the target by 50% for 6 sec.

talents.name: Weighted Edge
talents.text: Increases damage against slowed targets by 2/4/6%.

talents.name: Glacial Edge
talents.text: Increases the duration of Rime by 1/2/3 sec.

talents.name: Tempered
talents.text: Increases Strength by 1/2/3/4/5%.

talents.name: Rune Charge
talents.text: Melee attacks build a charge, up to five. Each grants 1/2/3/4/5 frost damage per swing.

talents.name: Cold Endurance
talents.text: Reduces damage taken while below 35% health by 5/10%.

talents.name: Cold Blood
talents.text: Increases critical strike chance by 1/2/3%.

talents.name: Shattering Blow
talents.text: Consumes all rune charges to deal frost damage scaled to the number consumed.

talents.name: Killing Frost
talents.text: Critical strikes against slowed targets restore 3/6/9 rage.

talents.name: Chillguard
talents.text: Reduces damage taken from slowed enemies by 2/4/6%.

talents.name: Frost Reserve
talents.text: Rune charges build 15/30% faster.

talents.name: Hoarfrost
talents.text: For 20 sec every swing deals additional frost damage and applies Rime automatically. Two minute cooldown.

talents.name: Numbing Cold
talents.text: Rime also reduces the target's attack speed by 5/10/15%.

talents.name: Deep Freeze
talents.text: Increases Shattering Blow damage by 15/30%.

talents.name: Permafrost
talents.text: Rune charges no longer decay out of combat, up to 1/2/3 retained.

talents.name: Bitter Cold
talents.text: Shattering Blow also slows all nearby enemies by 25/50%.

talents.name: Unbreakable Rime
talents.text: Rime can no longer be dispelled and its slow is 5/10/15% stronger.

talents.name: The Runeblade
talents.text: Requires an equipped runeblade. Your weapon permanently deals frost damage on every swing, your strikes always apply Rime, and killing blows restore rage.
talents.note: The only capstone in the document gated on an item rather than on points. It exists to close the loop with the forged verb: the capstone should not function without the thing that was forged.

trees.name: Survival
trees.concept: The close-range trapper. A hunter who fights beside the pet rather than behind it.
trees.localMechanic: Traps used offensively rather than defensively
trees.verbNote: A master, a trial, and a demonstration. The Beastmaster was a hero you hired rather than one you built.
trees.reworkNote: The only entry that reworks an existing tree rather than adding a fourth, which is why it is Tier 2 and does not need a fresh realm. Vanilla's Survival is already full of traps and melee-adjacent talents and is the weakest of the three precisely because it never committed to either.
trees.loreAnchor: Rexxar exists in Warcraft III and in vanilla, fights in melee alongside Misha, and is the archetype fully realized. A hunter tree that produces Rexxar is a tree that produces something the setting already contains.

talents.name: Savage Strikes
talents.text: Increases melee damage by 2/4/6/8/10%.

talents.name: Trap Mastery
talents.text: Increases trap effect duration by 10/20/30%.

talents.name: Hunter's Guile
talents.text: Increases Agility by 1/2/3/4/5%.

talents.name: Combat Trapping
talents.text: Traps may be laid while in combat.
talents.note: This one talent is the rework. Vanilla traps require leaving combat, which is why the tree never worked, and it is the difference between a defensive tool and an offensive one.

talents.name: Deflection
talents.text: Increases parry chance by 2/4%.

talents.name: Improved Traps
talents.text: Reduces the cooldown of all traps by 2/4/6 sec.

talents.name: Thick Hide
talents.text: Increases armor from items by 2/4/6/8/10%.

talents.name: Close Quarters
talents.text: Reduces the damage penalty at melee range and increases melee weapon skill by 1/2/3/4/5.

talents.name: Snare Expert
talents.text: Traps arm 50/100% faster.

talents.name: Surefooted
talents.text: Increases chance to hit by 1/2/3% and reduces snare duration by 10/20/30%.

talents.name: Harpoon
talents.text: Throw a line to an enemy within 25 yards and pull yourself to them. A melee hunter without a gap closer is not a melee hunter.

talents.name: Wyvern Venom
talents.text: Melee strikes against trapped targets apply a damage over time effect for 10/20/30%.

talents.name: Killer Instinct
talents.text: Increases critical strike chance by 1/2/3%.

talents.name: Entrapment
talents.text: Your traps root the target in place for 2/4 sec.

talents.name: Coordinated Assault
talents.text: Your melee strikes command your pet to strike the same target for bonus damage. Off the global cooldown.

talents.name: Resourcefulness
talents.text: Reduces the mana cost of melee abilities by 10/20/30%.

talents.name: Bestial Discipline
talents.text: Increases your pet's focus regeneration by 25/50%.

talents.name: Pack Instinct
talents.text: Your pet gains 5/10/15% of your attack power.

talents.name: Trapper's Cunning
talents.text: Reduces trap cooldowns by 15/30%.

talents.name: Ferocious Bond
talents.text: Coordinated Assault also heals your pet for 5/10/15% of the damage dealt.

talents.name: Hunt as One
talents.text: You and your pet share a single threat pool and a single target. Coordinated Assault triggers automatically on every third melee strike, and your pet's abilities are usable off your own cooldowns.

trees.name: Chronomancer
trees.concept: The mage who does not add health but returns it. Healing as reversion rather than restoration, built on a record of what a target used to be.
trees.retailSource: None directly. Closest is the Bronze Dragonflight's own fiction and the time-magic vocabulary Warcraft has used since Warcraft III.
trees.localMechanic: Echo, a recorded snapshot of an ally's health taken by your spells and spent to return them to it. Not a resource bar; it lives on the target.
trees.verbNote: The seventh verb, and the only one that is not an event. Anachronos does not teach the chain, he shows it. The quest Long Forgotten Memories already has a mortal look into a Crystalline Tear and watch something that already happened; the acquisition is recognising that one of those memories is yours.
trees.professionNote: Access to an enchanter rather than being one, per the soft-gate rule. Binding a moment into an object is what enchanting already does.
trees.permanentCost: Cannot be resurrected by another player. Returns unaided after a delay, at a position held earlier in the fight.
trees.loreAnchor: Anachronos has stood at the Caverns of Time in Tanaris since patch 1.9, gating access behind Brood of Nozdormu reputation and showing chosen mortals the sealing of Ahn'Qiraj through a Crystalline Tear in Silithus. Vanilla already contains a bronze dragon whose entire function is letting a mortal witness what already happened. Nothing needs inventing.

talents.name: Recollection
talents.text: Your spells record an Echo of an ally's health. Echoes persist through your own death; an Echo taken above 90% health is worth more; two Echoes may be held per ally; Echoes do not expire while you remain in combat.

talents.name: Borrowed Time
talents.text: Your heals may be cast before they are needed, landing three seconds later. The delay may be cancelled; a delayed heal landing on a full ally becomes an absorb; two may be in flight; a delayed heal whose target dies first returns to you as mana.

talents.name: Accelerate
talents.text: Spending an Echo hastens the ally's next action, then their attack speed, then shortens their next cooldown, then extends to anyone else you Echoed recently, then shortens their global cooldown once.

talents.name: Sand in the Glass
talents.text: Time spent not casting banks mana. The bank may be spent as a burst, shared with an ally you Echoed, and is not lost on taking damage.

talents.name: Dilation
talents.text: Blink leaves an Echo of your position. Returning to it restores the mana you held, then the health, and an ally may trigger the return.

talents.name: Temporal Anomaly
talents.text: Place a stationary field in which healing over time ticks at twice the rate.

talents.name: Regression
talents.text: Spending an Echo also removes one recently applied debuff, then returns the ally's threat to its recorded value, then restores mana as well as health, then doubles below 20% health, then is not consumed if the ally already sits at the Echo's value.

talents.name: Foresight
talents.text: You see damage already in flight. A shield cast on an ally with incoming damage absorbs more, and the shield's unspent remainder becomes an Echo.

talents.name: Stasis
talents.text: Suspend an ally in time. They take no damage, cannot act, and cannot be healed. Ends on command.

talents.name: Paradox
talents.text: Two Echoes on one ally may be merged, healing for the difference. A merged Echo cannot be dispelled, refunds mana on merging, and may be moved to another ally.

talents.name: Unwind
talents.text: Your damage spells slow an enemy's casting, then their cooldown recovery. The slow may be spent to hasten an ally, and a slowed enemy's damage arrives late rather than not at all.

talents.name: Chronal Bond
talents.text: The twenty-point mark. Your Echoes are shared with a second ally near the first.

talents.name: Arcane Continuum
talents.text: Cross-tree. Arcane Missiles apply an Echo to the lowest-health party member; Evocation restores an ally's mana as well as your own; Presence of Mind applies to your next heal. Every mage has all three, so the talent stands alone.

talents.name: Frozen Moment
talents.text: Cross-tree. Frost Nova applies Stasis to allies caught in it rather than rooting them; Ice Block leaves an Echo where you stood.

talents.name: Fixed Point
talents.text: Subtraction. Your Echoes never expire and always hold their ally's highest value this fight. You may no longer cast any damaging spell.

talents.name: Timeless
talents.text: Your heals cannot be interrupted, then cannot be dispelled, then refresh your Echoes on completion, then take a fresh Echo on a critical heal, then may record an Echo from an ally's shield value.

talents.name: Second Sunrise
talents.text: An ally you Echo gains an absorb equal to the gap between their current and recorded health. It decays over time and refreshes when the Echo does.

talents.name: Rewind
talents.text: Return an ally to the state they held ten seconds ago: their health, and one debuff removed. If they died inside that window, they return at that health. Five minute cooldown.

trees.name: Dreamer
trees.concept: The druid who does not visit the Emerald Dream but brings a piece of it here and holds ground with it.
trees.retailSource: None. Vanilla's four inactive Dream portals and the Dragons of Nightmare are the whole source.
trees.localMechanic: Threshold, a large persistent piece of the Dream planted on the ground. One at a time. Inside it the world behaves as it does in the Dream, and the Nightmare is the same mechanic inverted.
trees.verbNote: The ninth verb and the only passive one. You enter a Barrow Den, you sleep, and you do not wake for a long time. Naralex in Wailing Caverns is the cautionary version: a druid who did exactly this and woke into the Nightmare.
trees.professionNote: Access to a herbalist rather than being one. The chain needs living things gathered from all four portal groves, which is what herbalism already does.
trees.permanentCost: You never fully wake. Sleep and fear effects that would be resisted take hold instead, and effects that break on damage do not break for you.
trees.loreAnchor: Vanilla has four portals to the Emerald Dream, at Twilight Grove in Duskwood, Seradane in the Hinterlands, Dream Bough in Feralas, and Bough Shadow in Ashenvale. All four are inactive. The Dragons of Nightmare guarding them drop an object that quests to Keeper Remulos and proves to be Malfurion's ring, telling the player he is inside fighting the Nightmare. Four doors, bosses at each, a named person on the other side, and no way through. Nothing in vanilla asserts something and refuses to show it more completely.

talents.name: Threshold
talents.text: Plant a large, persistent piece of the Emerald Dream on the ground. Only one may exist at a time.

talents.name: Rooted Ground
talents.text: Allies in your Threshold regenerate; their heals over time tick faster; their bleeds do not; they cannot be dazed; leaving carries the regeneration for six seconds.

talents.name: Verdance
talents.text: Your Nature spells cause plants to take root where they land, healing allies who stand among them; the effect grows over time; it spreads along your Entangling Roots; it survives your death for twenty seconds.

talents.name: Nightmare
talents.text: You may plant the corrupted version of your Threshold instead, which weakens what stands in it rather than strengthening it.

talents.name: Dread
talents.text: Enemies in a Nightmare are slowed, heal for less, have their casts pushed back, cannot regain stealth, and suffer their own periodic damage twice as fast.

talents.name: Wakefulness
talents.text: You may move your Threshold rather than replanting it; it follows you slowly; moving does not interrupt you; two may exist briefly during a move; moving costs no mana; it may snap to an ally instead.

talents.name: Lucid
talents.text: You see stealth and invisibility within thirty yards.

talents.name: Communion
talents.text: Allies within thirty yards share a portion of your spell power, then your critical strike chance, then your armor, then one of your active buffs, then your Nature's Swiftness. Doubled for anyone standing in your Threshold.

talents.name: Overgrowth
talents.text: Your Nature spells leave briars where they land, damaging enemies who cross them, then rooting them briefly, then the root cannot be dispelled.

talents.name: Emerald Vigor
talents.text: An ally who holds position for five seconds gains an absorb, doubled if they are inside your Threshold.

talents.name: Terror
talents.text: Your Entangling Roots frighten instead of rooting a target already afraid; the fear is graded rather than binary, reducing damage dealt against immune targets; it spreads on death; it does not break on your damage; the target cannot be healed briefly.

talents.name: Tending
talents.text: Your Threshold is not destroyed by area damage, cannot be dispelled, persists fully through your death, and refreshes when an ally dies inside it.

talents.name: Grove of Ysera
talents.text: The mark. Your Threshold heals for a portion of all damage dealt inside it, by anyone, to anyone.

talents.name: Dreamwalk
talents.text: Cross-tree. Rejuvenation and Regrowth land at full effect anywhere inside your Threshold regardless of range; Moonfire refreshes on enemies standing in a Nightmare. Every druid has all three.

talents.name: Wildseed
talents.text: Cross-tree. Your Feral forms gain your Threshold's regeneration and cannot be rooted inside it.

talents.name: Deep Slumber
talents.text: Subtraction. Your Threshold is permanent and cannot be moved or destroyed. You may not leave it.

talents.name: The Waking World
talents.text: Your Threshold's effects reach the whole raid at half strength, then your party at full, then apply Dream and Nightmare simultaneously to the correct targets, then resurrect an ally who dies inside it once per fight, then double its size.

talents.name: Ysera's Regard
talents.text: Allies who leave your Threshold keep its effects for ten seconds, then twenty, then until they enter combat elsewhere.

talents.name: Open the Way
talents.text: Your Threshold becomes a portal for twenty seconds. Allies may step through and are untargetable, healed, and cleansed while inside, returning where they entered. You cannot enter it yourself.

trees.name: Radiance
trees.concept: The heretical Light. Healing and harm are one act, and the priest cannot do either alone.
trees.retailSource: None. Vanilla's Holy Nova is the whole source: a spell that heals and damages in one cast, buried in the Holy tree since launch.
trees.localMechanic: Corona. Your healing emits outward and damages what stands near its target; your damage emits outward and heals what stands near its. Nothing you cast affects only one thing.
trees.verbNote: The tenth verb. You publicly renounced the doctrine and the Light did not leave you. The chain is a trial rather than a lesson, and the only acquisition on the list where the character is tested and nothing is taken away.
trees.professionNote: Access to an enchanter. The trial requires a focus that survives being told it is heresy, which is a disenchanting problem.
trees.permanentCost: You can no longer cast Power Word: Shield or any absorb. You do not prevent.
trees.loreAnchor: Holy Nova has damaged enemies and healed allies in one cast since launch, sits in the Holy tree, is famously weak, and is taken by nobody. The fantasy of the Light as an act that comforts and sears at once has existed in the game since launch as a single bad spell with nothing built around it.

talents.name: Corona
talents.text: Your healing emits outward and damages nearby enemies; your damage emits outward and heals nearby allies.

talents.name: Effulgence
talents.text: The emission reaches further, cannot be resisted, ignores line of sight, prefers wounded allies and healthy enemies, and strikes a second ring at half effect.

talents.name: Kindling
talents.text: Your heals build a stack; at five your next emission doubles; stacks persist through target changes; overhealing builds two.

talents.name: Searing Mercy
talents.text: The damage half of your emission scales with the healing the cast did, then with overhealing specifically, then applies Holy Fire's burn, then cannot be reflected, then refreshes when the enemy takes further damage.

talents.name: Sanctuary
talents.text: The healing half of your emission scales with damage done, reaches your whole party, heals for the excess when an enemy dies inside it, and cleanses one effect.

talents.name: Holy Nova
talents.text: Rebuilt from vanilla's dead spell into the tree's rotational core: it costs less than a heal, emits at full value, and refreshes Kindling.

talents.name: Revelation
talents.text: Brand a target. Your emissions centre on the brand rather than on your cast.

talents.name: Doctrine
talents.text: Your emission may be aimed, then split between two points, then held for one global cooldown and released, then centred on an ally rather than yourself, then centred on a corpse.

talents.name: Unbroken
talents.text: Your casts cannot be pushed back while any ally is below half health, then while any enemy is branded, then at all during Absolution.

talents.name: Conflagrant Grace
talents.text: For ten seconds your healing lands at full value on allies and full damage on enemies with no falloff.

talents.name: Zealotry
talents.text: Critical heals critically damage, and the reverse; a critical builds two Kindling; criticals cannot be resisted; a critical on a branded target resets Revelation; two criticals in a row make your next cast instant.

talents.name: Penitence
talents.text: Healing yourself damages what is attacking you, then everything nearby, then applies your brand, then heals your attackers' targets.

talents.name: Congregation
talents.text: The mark. Your emissions also emit from every ally you healed in the last three seconds.

talents.name: Radiant Word
talents.text: Cross-tree. Smite and Holy Fire carry a full emission; Renew's ticks each emit at reduced value. Every priest has all three.

talents.name: Shadow's Mirror
talents.text: Cross-tree. Shadow Word: Pain's ticks emit healing; Mind Blast emits at full value.

talents.name: Apostasy
talents.text: Subtraction. Your emissions double in size and effect. You may no longer target allies with any spell, so all of your healing is emission and none of it is aimed.

talents.name: The Unquiet Light
talents.text: Your emission persists on the ground for three seconds, then follows the branded target, then leaves a trail as you move, then triggers again when the brand expires, then applies to everything your party heals.

talents.name: Litany
talents.text: Your spells apply a stacking mark to whatever they touch; at three stacks the next spell on that target is doubled; the mark transfers to a nearby target on death.

talents.name: Absolution
talents.text: For twelve seconds every point of healing you do is dealt again as holy damage to every enemy in range, and every point of damage you deal is healed again to every ally in range, with no falloff and no cap on targets.

sampleBuilds.description: A death knight who still tanks. Damnation plus enough Protection for defensive fundamentals.
A paladin who dabbled. Blood Rite as an emergency button in an otherwise Light-driven build, and the Blessings still work because Damnation was never taken.
A caster with three Risen and enough Frost for control.
A mage with a temporary skeleton and a real burst spec.
A healer who bonds a totem to the tank. Probably the most immediately popular build on this list.

openItems: Three acquisition chains are unspecified: Bladedancer, Conduit, and Survival. Section 8.6 names locations for the other four only.
Fist weapon itemization in vanilla is thin, and the Bladedancer weapon fork depends on it. Filling that lane in is additive Tier 1 work but it is a prerequisite rather than a nice-to-have.

Chronomancer gives mage two absorbed trees and therefore five in total, against four for every other host. Five is the stated ceiling. The justification is in chronomancer.md section 2 and rests on the talent audit rather than on symmetry.
